ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $C$, $D$ are two points on $\odot O$. If $\angle BAC=40^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $CB$, \\
$\because$ $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $\angle BAC = 40^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle BAC = 40^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBA = 50^\circ$, \\
$\because$ quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in $\odot O$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC + \angle CBA = 180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC = \boxed{130^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use arc measures and the inscribed angle theorem directly. From the image, observe that A and B are opposite endpoints of a diameter, C is on the upper-right part of the circle, and D is on the minor arc from A to C, so ∠ADC intercepts the arc AC that does not contain D, namely the large arc passing through B.
